hitl_conditions: Not discussed explicitly; humans remain recipients of recommendations (plant managers via dashboards/UI) and suppliers of domain expertise and expert opinions; RL agents trained in simulation are deployed to make real-time recommendations (no autonomous execution stated).
key_finding: Conceptual framing of process (factory/supply chain) digital twins as evolving, learning systems built on four elements (Data, Domain, Analytics, Outcome) and three functions (offline model development, real-time synchronization, online learning); discrete-event simulation augmented by ML surrogates, RL agents and computer vision describes, predicts and prescribes actions on factory/supply-chain KPIs.

quotes.text: We do not consider all simulations a digital twin because synchronization and learning are required for the simulations to serve as true digital twins.

Consequently, we would gain enhanced visibility not only into factory performance but also into the effectiveness of production, inventory, and delivery plans across the entire network of suppliers, plants, distribution centers, and customers.
quotes.section: 2. Factory and Supply Chain Twin Foundational Elements

quotes.text: Focusing on the role of simulation augmented by machine learning (ML) and reinforcement learning (RL), we touch on several challenges that arise in industrial twin use cases and how they can be overcome.
Once the training of the RL agents is completed, they can be deployed into the real environment where they make real-time recommendations about queue and resource control.
quotes.section: 7.4. Providing an Environment to Train Reinforcement Learning Agents

quotes.text: They are the actions that are recommended to control the factory floor and establish a closed feedback loop between physical and digital representations.
It helps to identify the key risk drivers and allows the plant manager to focus on the most critical inputs enabling effective factory control.
